t: You are standing where Old St Paul's Cathedral once stood, on Ludgate Hill. It was the cathedral of the City of London until the Great Fire of 1666. The building dates from 1087 and from 1255 to 1314, and it was perhaps the fourth church on this site, going back to the seventh century. Christopher Wren designed the cathedral that replaced it, completed in 1710. Burials here included Earconwald, Bishop of London from 675, and the Anglo-Saxon king Æthelred the Unready. John of Gaunt, father of Henry IV, was buried here too, and so was Edward the Exile.
